description: Each creature in a 10 ft radius sphere around a point within 90 ft makes a Wisdom save or is confused for up to 1 minute (concentration). It can't take reactions and rolls a d10 at the start of each turn:
1: It moves its full speed in a random direction (roll a d8) and takes no action.
2-6: It doesn't move or act.
7-8: It uses its action to melee attack a random creature in reach, or does nothing if none is in reach.
9-10: It moves and acts normally.
Each time it ends a turn it repeats the save, ending the effect on a success.
confusion.higherLevels: Each slot level above 4 widens the sphere by 5 ft.

description: Choose a 10 ft cube of air, earth, fire or water within 90 ft. A matching elemental of CR 5 or lower appears within 10 ft of it for up to 1 hour (concentration), vanishing at 0 HP.
It is friendly to your group, rolls its own initiative and obeys your spoken orders (no action needed); unordered, it only defends itself. The DM has its stats.
If your concentration breaks, it stays but turns hostile and may attack. You can't dismiss it; it vanishes 1 hour after you summoned it.
conjure-elemental.higherLevels: Each slot level above 5 raises the CR by 1.
conjure-elemental.material: Burning incense (air), soft clay (earth), sulfur and phosphorus (fire), or water and sand (water)

description: You reach out to a demigod, a long-dead sage's spirit or some other strange entity from another plane. Make a DC 15 Intelligence save.
Fail: you take 6d6 psychic damage and go insane until you finish a long rest: you can't take actions, understand speech or read, and you speak only gibberish. Greater restoration cures it.
Success: you may ask up to 5 questions while the spell lasts. Each gets a one-word reply (yes, no, maybe, never, irrelevant or unclear), or a short phrase if one word would mislead.

A fey creature of CR 6 or lower, or a fey spirit in the shape of a beast of CR 6 or lower, appears in a free space you can see within 90 ft. It vanishes at 0 HP or when the spell ends (concentration, up to 1 hour).
It is friendly to your group, rolls its own initiative and obeys your spoken orders (no action needed) if they fit its alignment; unordered, it only defends itself. The DM has its stats.
If your concentration breaks, it stays but turns hostile and may attack. You can't dismiss it; it vanishes 1 hour after you summoned it.
conjure-fey.higherLevels: Each slot level above 6 raises the CR by 1.

description: Elementals appear in free spaces you can see within 90 ft for up to 1 hour (concentration). Pick one option:
• 1 elemental of CR 2 or lower
• 2 elementals of CR 1 or lower
• 4 elementals of CR 1/2 or lower
• 8 elementals of CR 1/4 or lower

Each vanishes at 0 HP or when the spell ends. They are friendly to your group, act on one shared initiative and follow your spoken orders (no action needed); unordered, they only defend themselves. The DM has their stats.
conjure-minor-elementals.higherLevels: A 6th-level slot doubles the number summoned; an 8th-level slot triples it.

description: Shoot a nonmagical piece of ammunition or throw a nonmagical weapon at a point within 150 ft. Hundreds of copies rain down in a 40 ft radius, 20 ft high cylinder there, then vanish.
Each creature in the area makes a Dexterity save: 8d8 damage of the weapon's or ammunition's type, half on a success.
conjure-volley.material: A piece of ammunition or a thrown weapon

description: Fey creatures appear in free spaces you can see within 60 ft for up to 1 hour (concentration). Pick one option:
• 1 fey creature of CR 2 or lower
• 2 fey creatures of CR 1 or lower
• 4 fey creatures of CR 1/2 or lower
• 8 fey creatures of CR 1/4 or lower

Each vanishes at 0 HP or when the spell ends. They are friendly to your group, act on one shared initiative and follow your spoken orders (no action needed); unordered, they only defend themselves. The DM has their stats.
conjure-woodland-beings.higherLevels: A 6th-level slot doubles the number summoned; an 8th-level slot triples it.
conjure-woodland-beings.material: One holly berry for each creature summoned

description: Melee spell attack vs a creature in reach; on a hit it catches a disease you pick. At the end of each of its turns it makes a Constitution save: 3 failures lock it in for 7 days with no more saves; 3 successes cure it, ending the spell. Disease cures work.
Blinding Sickness: blinded; disadvantage on Wisdom checks and saves.
Filth Fever: disadvantage on Strength checks, saves and Strength attacks.
Flesh Rot: disadvantage on Charisma checks; vulnerable to all damage.
Mindfire: disadvantage on Intelligence checks and saves; acts as if confused in combat.
Seizure: disadvantage on Dexterity checks, saves and Dexterity attacks.
Slimy Doom: disadvantage on Constitution checks and saves; any damage stuns it until its next turn ends.
Choose a spell you can cast of 5th level or lower, with a casting time of 1 action, that can target you. Cast it together with this spell, spending both slots, and describe a trigger.

The stored spell takes effect on you alone the first time the trigger happens, whether you want it or not, and contingency ends. You can have only one contingency at a time; casting another ends the first. It also ends if the statuette isn't on you.
contingency.material: Ivory statuette of yourself set with gems, worth 1,500 gp

description: Control freestanding water in a cube up to 100 ft wide within 300 ft. Pick an effect now; later, as an action, repeat or switch:
Flood: still water rises up to 20 ft. In open water, a 20 ft wave crosses the area each turn instead, carrying Huge or smaller vehicles (25% capsize chance).
Part Water: the water splits into two walls around a trench.
Redirect Flow: the water moves the way you choose, even uphill.

Whirlpool (water 50 ft square, 25 ft deep): pulls things within 25 ft 10 ft closer. Entering or starting a turn there: Strength save or 2d8 bludgeoning and caught (half, free on a success). Swim out: Athletics vs your save DC (disadvantage if caught).
control-water.material: A drop of water and a pinch of dust

description: Cast only at night. Up to 3 Medium or Small humanoid corpses within 10 ft rise as ghouls under your control (the DM has their stats).
Bonus action: command any of them within 120 ft (one order for all); unordered, they just defend themselves. An order holds until the task is done.
Control lasts 24 hours. Recast before it ends to keep up to 3 of them for another 24 hours instead of making new ones.
create-undead.higherLevels: 7th-level slot: 4 ghouls. 8th: 5 ghouls or 2 ghasts or wights. 9th: 6 ghouls, 3 ghasts or wights, or 2 mummies.
create-undead.material: Per corpse: a clay pot of grave dirt, a clay pot of brackish water, and a black onyx stone worth 150 gp

description: Using Shadowfell shadow-stuff, you make a nonliving object of plant matter (cloth, rope, wood) or mineral (stone, crystal, metal) within 30 ft. It fits in a 5 ft cube and must be a form and material you have seen. How long it lasts depends on the material (mixed: use the shortest):
Vegetable matter: 1 day. Stone or crystal: 12 hours. Precious metals: 1 hour. Gems: 10 minutes. Adamantine or mithral: 1 minute.
Any spell that uses something made this way as its material component fails.
creation.higherLevels: Each slot level above 5 grows the cube by 5 ft.
creation.material: A tiny bit of the same matter as the item

description: You touch a creature and shield it for 8 hours. The first time damage would drop it to 0 HP, it stays at 1 HP and the spell ends.
If it is still active when an effect would kill the target outright without dealing damage, that effect fails against it and the spell ends.
You strike the ground and divine force ripples out. Each creature you choose within 30 ft makes a Constitution save.
Fail: 5d6 thunder plus 5d6 radiant or necrotic (your choice), and it falls prone. Success: half damage, and it stays standing.
You teleport to any spot within 500 ft that you can see, picture, or describe by distance and direction ("200 ft straight down").
You can take objects you can carry, plus one willing creature your size or smaller within 5 ft, with its gear up to its carrying capacity.
If the arrival space is occupied, you and anyone with you take 4d6 force damage and stay put.
A green ray hits a target you can see within 60 ft: a creature, an object, or something made of magical force (such as a wall of force).
A creature makes a Dexterity save or takes 10d6 + 40 force. If that drops it to 0 HP, it turns to gray dust with all it carries except magic items; only true resurrection or wish can revive it.
A Large or smaller nonmagical object or force creation is destroyed outright; a bigger one loses a 10 ft cube. Magic items are unaffected.
disintegrate.material: A lodestone and a pinch of dust

description: For up to 1 minute (concentration), attacks by celestials, elementals, fey, fiends and undead against you have disadvantage. Either option below also ends the spell:
Break Enchantment: as an action, touch a creature you can reach to free it from being charmed, frightened or possessed by one of those creature types.

Dismissal: as an action, make a melee spell attack against one of those creatures in reach. On a hit it makes a Charisma save or is sent to its home plane (undead to the Shadowfell, fey to the Feywild if already home).
dispel-evil-and-good.material: Holy water or powdered silver and iron

description: With an offering, you ask a god or its servants one question about a goal, event or activity happening within 7 days. The DM answers truthfully, maybe as a brief phrase, a riddle-like rhyme or an omen. It ignores later changes, like new spells or allies lost.
Each casting after the first before your next long rest has a cumulative 25% chance of a random reading, rolled secretly by the DM.
divination.material: Incense and a fitting sacrificial offering, together worth 25 gp, used up

description: A beast you can see within 60 ft makes a Wisdom save (advantage if you or your allies are fighting it) or is charmed by you for up to 1 minute (concentration).

While on the same plane, you can give it simple orders telepathically (no action needed) and it does its best to obey; with no new orders it defends itself. As an action, take full control until the end of your next turn: it does only what you choose, and you can spend your reaction to make it use its own.
Each time it takes damage it repeats the save, ending the spell on a success.
dominate-beast.higherLevels: Concentration rises to 10 minutes with a 5th-level slot, 1 hour with 6th, and 8 hours with 7th or higher.

description: A humanoid you can see within 60 ft makes a Wisdom save (advantage if you or your allies are fighting it) or is charmed by you for up to 1 minute (concentration).

While on the same plane, you can give it simple orders telepathically (no action needed) and it does its best to obey; with no new orders it defends itself. As an action, take full control until the end of your next turn: it does only what you choose, and you can spend your reaction to make it use its own.
Each time it takes damage it repeats the save, ending the spell on a success.
dominate-person.higherLevels: Concentration rises to 10 minutes with a 6th-level slot, 1 hour with 7th, and 8 hours with 8th or higher.

description: You mark an object of 10 pounds or less, no longer than 6 ft, and its name appears invisibly on the sapphire. Each casting needs a new sapphire.

Later, as an action, speak its name and crush the gem: it lands in your hand from any distance, even across planes, and the spell ends. If someone else holds or carries it, it stays put but you learn who has it and roughly where.
Dispel magic or similar on the sapphire ends the spell.

Target a creature you know on your plane (not one that doesn't sleep, like an elf). You, or a willing creature you touch, fall into a trance as the messenger, aware of your surroundings but unable to move or act.

While the target sleeps, the messenger appears in its dreams to talk and shape the dream; the target remembers it all. If it is awake, wait for sleep or end the spell. The messenger can leave the trance at any time.
Nightmare: deliver up to 10 words, then the target makes a Wisdom save (disadvantage if you have a piece of its body). Fail: it gains no benefit from that rest and takes 3d6 psychic on waking.
dream.material: Sand, ink, and a quill taken from a sleeping bird

description: Black tentacles fill a 20 ft square of ground you can see within 90 ft for up to 1 minute (concentration), making it difficult terrain.

A creature entering it for the first time on a turn, or starting its turn there, makes a Dexterity save or takes 3d6 bludgeoning and is restrained until the spell ends. One already restrained takes 3d6 bludgeoning when its turn starts there.
A restrained creature can use its action for a Strength or Dexterity check (its pick) against your spell save DC to break free.
evards-black-tentacles.material: A bit of tentacle from a giant octopus or giant squid

description: Your eyes turn to dark voids for up to 1 minute (concentration). On casting and as an action each later turn, a creature you can see within 60 ft makes a Wisdom save or suffers your chosen effect. A creature that succeeded can't be targeted again.
Asleep: unconscious until it takes damage or someone uses an action to wake it.
Panicked: frightened; on each turn it Dashes away from you by the safest short route unless trapped, until it is 60 ft or more away and can't see you.
Sickened: disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks. It repeats the save as each of its turns ends, ending this on a success.

You turn raw materials you can see within 120 ft into a finished item of the same stuff, such as trees into a wooden bridge or hemp into rope. The item can be Large or smaller (fitting a 10 ft cube or eight joined 5 ft cubes), or Medium at most (one 5 ft cube) for metal, stone or other minerals.
Quality matches the raw materials. You can't make or change creatures or magic items, and fine work like jewelry, weapons, glass or armor needs proficiency with the matching artisan's tools.

Name a fixed place on your plane that you know. For up to 1 day (concentration), while on its plane, you know its distance and direction, and at every fork you know which way is shortest and most direct, though not always safest.
The spell fails for a place on another plane, one that moves (like a mobile fortress), or a vague one ("a green dragon's lair").
find-the-path.material: Divining tools (bones, cards, runes or similar) worth 100 gp, plus an item taken from the destination

description: Wispy flames surround you for 10 minutes, giving bright light to 10 ft and dim light 10 ft beyond. You can end it early as an action.
Warm shield: resistance to cold damage. Chill shield: resistance to fire damage.
When a creature within 5 ft hits you with a melee attack, it takes 2d8 fire (warm) or 2d8 cold (chill).
fire-shield.material: A bit of phosphorus or a firefly

description: Holy fire pours down in a 10 ft radius, 40 ft high cylinder around a point within 60 ft. Each creature in it makes a Dexterity save: 4d6 fire plus 4d6 radiant, half on a success.
flame-strike.higherLevels: Each slot level above 5 adds 1d6 to the fire or the radiant damage (your pick).

description: A creature you can see within 60 ft, with a body of flesh, makes a Constitution save. On a failure it is restrained as it starts to harden.
While restrained, it repeats the save at the end of each of its turns. 3 successes (not necessarily in a row) end the spell; 3 failures turn it to stone, petrified for the duration.
If you keep concentration for the full minute, it stays stone until the effect is removed. Breaking the statue leaves matching injuries if it is restored.
flesh-to-stone.material: A pinch of lime, water and earth

description: You ward up to 40,000 sq ft of floor, 30 ft high, for 1 day. Nothing can teleport in or enter by portal (like gate), the Astral or Ethereal Plane, the Feywild, the Shadowfell or plane shift.

Choose creature types from celestials, elementals, fey, fiends and undead. One of them entering the area for the first time on a turn, or starting its turn there, takes 5d10 radiant or necrotic (your choice when cast). A password you set spares the speaker.
Areas can't overlap another forbiddance. Casting it in the same place daily for 30 days makes it last until dispelled; the last casting uses up the materials.
forbiddance.material: Holy water, rare incense, and 1,000 gp of powdered ruby

description: For 1 hour, a willing creature you touch ignores difficult terrain, and no spell or magical effect can lower its speed, paralyze it or restrain it.
It can spend 5 ft of movement to slip free of nonmagical restraints, such as manacles or a grapple. Being underwater doesn't hamper its movement or attacks.
freedom-of-movement.material: A leather strap tied around an arm or similar limb

description: Give a command to a creature you can see within 60 ft that understands you: do some service, or avoid some act. It makes a Wisdom save or is charmed by you for 30 days. Each time it directly works against your order it takes 5d10 psychic, at most once a day.
Any order is allowed except one meaning certain death; a suicidal order ends the spell. You can end it as an action; remove curse, greater restoration or wish also ends it.
geas.higherLevels: A 7th- or 8th-level slot makes it last 1 year; a 9th-level slot makes it last until one of those spells ends it.

description: Within 30 ft, up to 10 centipedes, 3 spiders, 5 wasps or 1 scorpion grow into giant versions for up to 10 minutes (concentration). The DM may allow other bugs, like a bee becoming a giant wasp.
They obey your spoken commands and act on your turn in combat; the DM has their stats and runs their actions and movement.
Each stays giant until the spell ends, it drops to 0 HP, or you use an action to end it for that creature.
A still, shimmering barrier forms in a 10 ft radius around you for up to 1 minute (concentration).

Spells cast from outside at 5th level or lower can't affect creatures or objects inside, even if cast with a higher slot. They can still target things inside, but do nothing, and their areas leave the inside untouched.
globe-of-invulnerability.higherLevels: Each slot level above 6 blocks spells one level higher.
globe-of-invulnerability.material: A glass or crystal bead that breaks when the spell ends

description: A vine sprouts in a free space you can see within 30 ft for up to 1 minute (concentration). When you cast it, it lashes at a creature you can see within 30 ft of it: Dexterity save or be pulled 20 ft straight toward the vine.
Bonus action on each of your turns: lash at the same creature or a new one.

You or a creature you touch turns invisible for up to 1 minute (concentration), along with what it wears and carries while on its person. Unlike invisibility, attacking or casting spells doesn't end it.
Touch a creature to remove one exhaustion level or end one of these:
• one effect charming or petrifying it
• one curse, including attunement to a cursed magic item
• any reduction to one of its ability scores
• one effect reducing its hit point maximum
greater-restoration.material: Diamond dust worth 100 gp, used up

description: A Large spectral guardian with your deity's sword and shield fills a free space you can see within 30 ft for 8 hours.
Any creature hostile to you that first moves within 10 ft of it on a turn makes a Dexterity save: 20 radiant damage, half on a success. The guardian disappears once it has dealt 60 damage in total.

Ward up to 2,500 sq ft of floor, up to 20 ft tall, any shape, for 24 hours, split across floors you walk while casting if you like. Name creatures it ignores, plus an optional password protecting its speaker.
Corridors: fog heavily obscures them; at each junction others have a 50% chance of heading the wrong way.
Doors: arcane-locked; up to 10 can look like plain wall.
Stairs: webbed (as web), regrowing within 10 minutes if cleared.
Plus one: dancing lights in 4 corridors, magic mouth or stinking cloud in 2 places, gust of wind in one room, or suggestion in a 5 ft square.
Dispel magic removes one effect per success. Recast daily for a year: permanent.
guards-and-wards.material: Burning incense, brimstone and oil, knotted string, umber hulk blood, and a silver rod worth 10 gp

description: Over 24 hours you charge a radius up to 60 ft around a touched point (not overlapping another hallow). Celestials, elementals, fey, fiends and undead are barred from entering and from charming, frightening or possessing anyone inside; such effects end on entering. You may exempt types.
Add one effect, for everyone or a group you name (a deity's followers, orcs). A creature entering or starting its turn there may make a Charisma save to ignore it until it leaves.

Courage: no frightened. Darkness or Daylight (beats lower-level magic). Energy Protection or Vulnerability: one type, not bludgeoning, piercing or slashing. Everlasting Rest: dead can't become undead. Extradimensional Interference: no teleport or planar travel. Fear: frightened inside. Silence. Tongues: shared understanding.
hallow.material: Herbs, oils and incense worth 1,000 gp, used up

description: Natural terrain in a 150 ft cube within 300 ft looks, sounds and smells like other natural terrain for 24 hours: a road can seem a swamp, a cliff a gentle slope. Buildings, gear and creatures look unchanged.

Touch isn't fooled, so anyone walking in likely sees through it. If touch doesn't reveal it, a creature studying it closely can roll Investigation vs your spell save DC; success shows it only as a faint image over the real ground.
hallucinatory-terrain.material: Stone, twig, and some green plant

description: A creature you can see within 60 ft makes a Constitution save: 14d6 necrotic, half on a success. This can't drop it below 1 HP.
On a failure, its hit point maximum also drops by the damage taken for 1 hour. Anything that cures disease restores the maximum early.
A creature you can see within 60 ft regains 70 HP, and any blindness, deafness and diseases on it end. Constructs and undead are unaffected.
heal.higherLevels: Each slot level above 6 heals 10 more HP.

description: Conjure a banquet for yourself and as many as 12 other creatures. The meal takes 1 hour to eat, then vanishes, and only then do its benefits start.

For the next 24 hours each diner is free of all disease and poison, can't be poisoned or frightened, and makes every Wisdom save with advantage. Roll 2d10: its hit point maximum grows by that much, and its current hit points rise by the same amount.
A creature you can see within 90 ft makes a Wisdom save or is paralyzed for up to 1 minute (concentration). Undead are unaffected.
It repeats the save as each of its turns ends, breaking free on a success.
hold-monster.higherLevels: Each slot level above 5 adds a target; all must be within 30 ft of each other.
hold-monster.material: A small straight piece of iron

description: Hard hail pounds a 20 ft radius, 40 ft high cylinder around a point within 300 ft. Each creature in it makes a Dexterity save: 2d8 bludgeoning plus 4d6 cold, half on a success.
Until your next turn ends, the area is difficult terrain.
ice-storm.higherLevels: Each slot level above 4 adds 1d8 bludgeoning.
ice-storm.material: Some dust and a little water

description: Biting locusts fill a 20 ft radius sphere around a point within 300 ft for up to 10 minutes (concentration). It spreads around corners, is lightly obscured and is difficult terrain.
Each creature in it when it appears makes a Constitution save: 4d10 piercing, half on a success. A creature also saves the first time each turn it enters, and whenever it ends its turn there.
insect-plague.material: Some sugar grains, grain kernels and a smear of fat

description: Pick a person, place or object by name or description, and a short summary of its notable lore comes to mind: current tales, forgotten stories, even secrets. Things of no legendary importance give nothing.
The more you already know about it, the more precise the result. The lore is true but may come as riddling or poetic language.
legend-lore.material: Incense worth 250 gp (used up) and 4 ivory strips worth 50 gp each

description: Touch the chest and its replica to hide the chest and contents (up to 12 cubic ft of nonliving matter) on the Ethereal Plane.
Action, touching the replica: the chest appears on the ground within 5 ft. Action, touching both: send it back.

From day 60, each day adds a cumulative 5% chance the spell ends. Recasting, losing the replica, or ending it as an action also ends it. If the chest is on the Ethereal Plane then, it is lost for good.
leomunds-secret-chest.material: A 3 by 2 by 2 ft chest of rare materials worth 5,000 gp and a Tiny replica worth 50 gp

description: For up to 1 hour (concentration) you sense the direction of a creature you name or describe, if it is within 1,000 ft, and which way it moves.

It finds a specific creature you know, or the nearest of a kind (like a human or a unicorn) if you have seen one within 30 ft at least once. It fails if the creature is in another form (such as polymorphed) or running water 10 ft wide lies directly between you.
Your soul enters the container; your body goes catatonic. You perceive from there but can't move or react. Only action: send your soul up to 100 ft, home (ending the spell) or into a humanoid.
Possess: a humanoid you can see within 100 ft makes a Charisma save (protection from evil and good or magic circle blocks it). Fail: souls swap. Success: no retry for 24 hours.
You use the host's stats but keep your alignment, Int, Wis, Cha and class features. Action: return to the container within 100 ft.
Host dies: Charisma save vs your DC, or you die. Container breaks or spell ends: you return to your body, dying if it is dead or over 100 ft away.
magic-jar.material: A gem, crystal, reliquary or other ornate container worth 500 gp

description: Choose up to 6 creatures in a 30 ft radius sphere around a point within 60 ft. Each regains 3d8 + your spellcasting modifier HP. Constructs and undead are unaffected.

Up to 12 creatures you can see within 60 ft that can hear and understand you make a Wisdom save (immune to charm: unaffected). On a failure, each follows a reasonable-sounding course of action you propose in a sentence or two, for up to 24 hours or until it's done.
An obviously harmful order, like stabbing itself, fails. You can set a trigger for the act; if it never happens, nothing is done. Damage from you or your companions frees that creature.
mass-suggestion.higherLevels: Lasts 10 days with a 7th-level slot, 30 days with 8th, and a year and a day with 9th.
mass-suggestion.material: A snake's tongue plus honeycomb or a drop of sweet oil

description: You turn invisible and an illusory double appears where you stand, for up to 1 hour (concentration). Attacking or casting a spell ends your invisibility; the double remains.
Action: move the double up to twice your speed, making it gesture, talk and act as you like.
You can see and hear through it as if there. Bonus action each turn: switch between its senses and yours; while on its senses you are blind and deaf to your own surroundings.

A creature you can see within 30 ft makes a Wisdom save (advantage if you're fighting it) or is charmed for up to 1 minute (concentration): incapacitated and oblivious to all but your voice. Damage or another spell targeting it ends the spell with no change.
While charmed, describe changes to an event from the last 24 hours that lasted 10 minutes or less: erase, sharpen, alter or invent. It must understand you; the change holds only if you finish first.
A false memory may not change behaviour; absurd ones are dismissed. Remove curse or greater restoration undoes it.
modify-memory.higherLevels: Reach older events: 7 days at 6th level, 30 days at 7th, 1 year at 8th, any time at 9th.

description: An invisible phantom watchdog sits in a free space you can see within 30 ft for 8 hours. It ends if you dismiss it (action) or move over 100 ft away. Only you see it; it can't be harmed.
It barks loudly if a Small or larger creature gets within 30 ft without saying your password. It sees invisible things and into the Ethereal Plane, and ignores illusions.
As each of your turns begins it bites a hostile creature within 5 ft: attack bonus = spellcasting modifier + proficiency bonus, 4d8 piercing.
mordenkainens-faithful-hound.material: A tiny silver whistle, a bit of bone and a thread

description: You secure a cube from 5 to 100 ft on a side within 120 ft for 24 hours, or until you end it as an action. Pick any of these:
• Sound can't cross the edge.
• The edge looks dark and foggy, blocking sight and darkvision.
• Divination sensors can't appear inside or pass through the edge.
• Divination spells can't target creatures inside.
• No teleporting in or out.
• No planar travel inside.
Casting it on the same spot daily for a year makes it permanent.
mordenkainens-private-sanctum.higherLevels: Each slot level above 4 adds 100 ft to the cube's side (200 ft at 5th).
mordenkainens-private-sanctum.material: Thin lead sheet, opaque glass, cotton or cloth, and powdered chrysolite

description: For up to 2 hours (concentration) you reshape dirt, sand or clay in an area up to 40 ft on a side within 120 ft: raise or lower ground, dig or fill a trench, build or flatten a wall, form a pillar. Changes can reach half the area's largest side (20 ft for a 40 ft square) and take 10 minutes to finish.
Every 10 minutes of concentration you may pick a new area. The slow change rarely traps or hurts creatures.
Natural stone and stonework can't be shaped, though they shift with the ground, and unstable buildings may collapse. Plants ride along with the moved earth.
move-earth.material: An iron blade and a small bag of mixed clay, loam and sand

description: A globe of cold bursts in a 60 ft radius sphere at a point within 300 ft. Each creature there makes a Constitution save: 10d6 cold, half on a success.
If it hits water, the surface freezes 6 inches deep over a 30 ft square for 1 minute, trapping swimmers; one can use an action for a Strength check vs your spell save DC to break out.
Or keep it as a sling-stone globe. You or someone you hand it to can throw it (40 ft) or sling it; it bursts on impact as above. It explodes on its own after 1 minute.
A force sphere encloses a Large or smaller creature or object within 30 ft for up to 1 minute (concentration). An unwilling creature makes a Dexterity save to avoid it.
Nothing passes in or out, though the creature inside can breathe. The sphere takes no damage, and no attack or effect crosses it either way. Disintegrate destroys it without harming what's inside.
The weightless sphere can be lifted by others, or rolled from inside as an action at up to half the creature's speed.
otilukes-resilient-sphere.material: Two half-spheres, one of clear crystal and one of gum arabic

description: A creature you can see within 30 ft starts dancing in place for up to 1 minute (concentration); there is no save to resist it at first. Creatures immune to charm are unaffected.
While dancing it spends all its movement dancing without leaving its space, has disadvantage on Dexterity saves and attack rolls, and attacks against it have advantage.
As an action, it can make a Wisdom save to stop; success ends the spell.
A passage up to 5 ft wide, 8 ft tall and 20 ft deep opens for 1 hour at a point you can see within 30 ft on wood, plaster or stone (wall, ceiling or floor). It doesn't weaken the structure around it.
When it closes, anything still inside is pushed safely out to the nearest free space by the surface you cast it on.
A creature you can see within 120 ft sees its worst fear, visible only to it. It makes a Wisdom save or is frightened for up to 1 minute (concentration).
At the start of each of its turns while frightened, it makes another Wisdom save: failure deals 4d10 psychic; success ends the spell.

You call on a powerful being you know (a god, primordial, demon prince or similar). It sends a loyal celestial, elemental or fiend to a free space within 60 ft. You may request one by name, but the DM may send another.

It owes you nothing; you bargain for a task and payment. Rough guide: 100 gp per minute, 1,000 gp per hour, 10,000 gp per day (up to 10 days). Fitting tasks may cost half or nothing, safe ones half, risky ones more; suicidal tasks are rarely accepted.
It leaves when done or when the term ends. With no deal it returns home at once. While serving it counts as a party member for XP.

A celestial, elemental, fey or fiend that stays within 60 ft for the whole hour of casting (often held in a reversed magic circle) makes a Charisma save. On a failure it serves you for 24 hours. If another spell summoned or made it, that spell lasts as long as this one.
It follows your instructions as well as it can, but a hostile one twists your words. If done early, it reports to you on your plane, or waits where you bound it.
planar-binding.higherLevels: Duration: 10 days at 6th level, 30 days at 7th, 180 days at 8th, a year and a day at 9th.
planar-binding.material: A jewel worth 1,000 gp, used up

description: A creature you can see within 60 ft turns into a beast with CR no higher than its level or CR, for up to 1 hour (concentration). An unwilling target makes a Wisdom save to resist; shapechangers succeed automatically.
It takes the beast's stats, mental scores included, keeping only alignment and personality. Gear melds in and can't be used. It can't speak, cast spells, or do anything needing hands or speech.
It uses the beast's HP. At 0 HP it reverts with its old HP, and excess damage carries over; it ends early if the target dies.

You set up a hidden illusion of an object, creature or other visible thing, up to a 30 ft cube, within 120 ft. Choose its sounds and actions (up to 5 minutes long) and a trigger based on what can be seen or heard within 30 ft of the area, such as a spoken password.
When triggered it plays out, then goes dormant for 10 minutes before it can trigger again. It lasts until dispelled.
Touching it shows it's fake. As an action, a creature can study it with Investigation vs your spell save DC; on a success it sees through it and its noises sound hollow.
programmed-illusion.material: Fleece, plus 25 gp of jade dust

description: Touch a creature dead no longer than 10 days. If its soul is willing and free, it returns with 1 HP. Poisons and nonmagical diseases it had are cured; magical diseases and curses stay unless removed first.
Mortal wounds close but lost body parts don't regrow; without a vital part, like the head, the spell fails. Undead can't be raised.
The target takes a -4 penalty to attack rolls, saves and ability checks, shrinking by 1 after each long rest.
raise-dead.material: A diamond worth 500 gp, used up

description: Up to 8 willing creatures you choose within 30 ft are linked telepathically for 1 hour. Creatures with Intelligence 2 or lower can't join.
Linked creatures can talk mind to mind at any distance, with or without a shared language, but not across planes.
rarys-telepathic-bond.material: Eggshell from two different kinds of creature

description: Touch a dead humanoid, or a piece of one, dead no more than 10 days. If its soul is free and willing, a new adult body forms and it returns to life. It keeps its memories and abilities but swaps its race and racial traits for the new one's.

The DM picks the new race or rolls d100: 01-04 dragonborn, 05-13 hill dwarf, 14-21 mountain dwarf, 22-25 dark elf, 26-34 high elf, 35-42 wood elf, 43-46 forest gnome, 47-52 rock gnome, 53-56 half-elf, 57-60 half-orc, 61-68 lightfoot halfling, 69-76 stout halfling, 77-96 human, 97-00 tiefling.
reincarnate.material: Rare oils and unguents worth 1,000 gp, used up

description: Choose a creature on your plane to watch and hear for up to 10 minutes (concentration). It makes a Wisdom save, or may fail on purpose. On a success it's unaffected, and you can't scry it again for 24 hours.
Save modifiers: heard of it +5, met it +0, know it well -5; likeness or picture -2, possession or garment -4, body part such as hair or nail -10.

On a failure an invisible sensor follows within 10 ft of it, and you see and hear through it. Creatures that see invisible things see a fist-sized glowing orb. You can instead target a place you have seen; the sensor stays put there.
scrying.material: A focus worth 1,000 gp, such as a crystal ball, silver mirror or font of holy water

description: Give any number of creatures you can see within 30 ft a new illusory look for 8 hours, or until you end it as an action. An unwilling target can make a Charisma save to avoid it.
You can change looks, clothing, armor, weapons and gear, and make each up to 1 ft shorter or taller, thinner or heavier. The body shape and limbs must stay the same.
The disguise fails to touch. As an action, a creature can make an Investigation check vs your spell save DC to spot it.
Your next melee weapon hit before the spell ends (concentration, up to 1 minute) deals an extra 4d6 psychic damage.
The target then makes a Wisdom save. On a failure, until its next turn ends it can't take reactions and rolls attacks and ability checks with disadvantage.

Touch a Medium or smaller stone object, or a piece of stone up to 5 ft in every dimension, and mold it into any shape: a weapon, idol or coffer, a passage through a wall under 5 ft thick, or a sealed-up door.
The result can have at most 2 hinges and a latch; finer moving parts aren't possible.
stone-shape.material: Soft clay, roughly shaped like the result

description: Harden a willing creature's flesh with a touch. For up to 1 hour (concentration) it resists bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage, as long as that damage comes from nonmagical attacks.
stoneskin.material: Diamond dust worth 100 gp, used up

description: For up to 1 minute (concentration) you can fire a 5 ft wide, 60 ft long line of light from your hand: once on casting, then as an action on later turns.
Each creature in the line makes a Constitution save: 6d8 radiant and blinded until your next turn, or half damage and not blinded on a success. Undead and oozes save with disadvantage.
Your hand glows with sunlight meanwhile: bright light to 30 ft, dim light 30 ft further.

Your quiver makes endless nonmagical ammunition for up to 1 minute (concentration). Each of your turns, as a bonus action, you can make 2 attacks with a weapon using its ammunition. Each piece fired is replaced.
The made ammunition crumbles when the spell ends. It also ends if the quiver leaves your possession.
swift-quiver.material: A quiver holding at least 1 piece of ammunition

description: For up to 10 minutes (concentration), on casting and as your action each round, you grip one creature or object you can see within 60 ft. Keep the target or switch; the old one is freed.

Creature (Huge or smaller): your spellcasting ability check vs its Strength. Win to move it up to 30 ft any direction within range; it is restrained (and hangs if lifted) until your next turn ends. Win again each round to hold it.
Object (up to 1,000 pounds): unattended, it moves up to 30 ft automatically; worn or carried, win the same contest to pull it away. Fine work, like using a tool or opening a door, is possible.

Inscribe a 10 ft wide circle of sigils that links to a permanent teleportation circle on your current plane, one whose sigil sequence you know. A portal shimmers open until your next turn ends; whoever enters arrives within 5 ft of the destination circle, or in the closest free space.

When you first gain the spell you know 2 sequences for Material Plane circles, chosen by the DM, and 1 minute of study lets you memorise any new one you find. Cast it at one spot every day for a year to create a permanent circle there.
teleportation-circle.material: Gem-infused inks and rare chalks worth 50 gp, consumed

description: Link a Large or larger inanimate plant within 10 ft to another plant anywhere on your plane, one you've seen or touched before.
Until the end of your next turn, any creature can spend 5 ft of movement to step into the first plant and out of the other.

For up to 1 minute (concentration), spend 5 ft of movement to enter a living tree at least your size. You sense all trees of that kind within 500 ft and, with the same move, can pass into one or step back out.
You exit within 5 ft of the destination tree for another 5 ft of movement (with none left, you exit by the tree you entered). Once per round; end each turn outside a tree.
A willing creature you touch gains truesight for 1 hour: within 120 ft it sees things as they truly are, notices secret doors hidden by magic, and sees into the Ethereal Plane.
true-seeing.material: Eye ointment of mushroom powder, saffron and fat worth 25 gp, used up

description: An opaque wall of fire stands on a solid surface within 120 ft for up to 1 minute (concentration): up to 60 ft long, 20 ft high and 1 ft thick, or a ring up to 20 ft across, 20 ft high and 1 ft thick.
Creatures in it when it appears make a Dexterity save: 5d8 fire, half on a success.
Choose one side. A creature ending its turn within 10 ft of that side or inside the wall takes 5d8 fire, as does one entering it for the first time on a turn. The other side is harmless.

An invisible, 1/4 inch thick wall of force appears within 120 ft for up to 10 minutes (concentration), at any angle, floating or resting. Shape it as a dome or sphere up to 10 ft in radius, or as ten 10 by 10 ft panels, each touching another. Creatures in its path are pushed to a side you pick.
Nothing physical gets through, and it reaches into the Ethereal Plane. It takes no damage and dispel magic doesn't work, but disintegrate destroys it at once.
wall-of-force.material: Powder from a crushed clear gemstone

description: A 1 ft thick ice wall forms on a solid surface within 120 ft for up to 10 minutes (concentration): a dome or sphere up to 10 ft in radius, or ten 10 ft square panels, each touching another.
A creature in its space is pushed to one side and makes a Dexterity save: 10d6 cold, half on a success.

Each 10 ft section has AC 12 and 30 HP and is vulnerable to fire. A destroyed section leaves frigid air; crossing it the first time on a turn calls for a Constitution save: 5d6 cold, half on a success.
wall-of-ice.higherLevels: Each slot level above 6 adds 2d6 to the first blast and 1d6 to the frigid air.

description: A nonmagical stone wall appears within 120 ft for up to 10 minutes (concentration): ten 10 by 10 ft panels 6 inches thick, or 10 by 20 ft panels 3 inches thick, each touching another. It needs no foundation but must join existing stone, so it can bridge gaps or form ramps; spans over 20 ft need half-size panels as supports.
Creatures in its path are pushed aside. One about to be fully enclosed makes a Dexterity save; success lets it use its reaction to move up to its speed out.
Each panel has AC 15 and 30 HP per inch of thickness. If you concentrate the full 10 minutes, it becomes permanent and can't be dispelled.

A wall of thorny brush grows on a solid surface within 120 ft for up to 10 minutes (concentration), blocking sight: up to 60 ft long, 10 ft high and 5 ft thick, or a ring 20 ft across, up to 20 ft high and 5 ft thick.
Creatures in it when it appears make a Dexterity save: 7d8 piercing, half on a success.
Moving through costs 4 ft per 1 ft. Entering it the first time on a turn or ending a turn there calls for a Dexterity save: 7d8 slashing, half on a success.
wall-of-thorns.higherLevels: Each slot level above 6 adds 1d8 to both kinds of damage.

description: You and up to 10 willing creatures you can see within 30 ft turn into wisps of cloud for 8 hours: flying speed 300 ft and resistance to damage from nonmagical weapons. In this form the only actions are Dash or changing back.
Switching form either way takes 1 minute, during which the creature is incapacitated and can't move.
If the spell ends while one is flying as a cloud, it sinks 60 ft per round for 1 minute and lands safely; if it hasn't landed by then, it falls the rest of the way.
You and up to 5 willing creatures within 5 ft teleport to your prepared sanctuary, arriving in the nearest free spaces to the spot you chose.
Prepare a sanctuary by casting this spell in a place dedicated to or tied to your deity, such as a temple. Cast anywhere else, or without a sanctuary, it does nothing.
Any number of willing creatures you can see within 30 ft each become a Large or smaller beast of CR 4 or lower; each can get a different form. On later turns, your action gives them new forms.

Each keeps its alignment and its Int, Wis and Cha, but uses the beast's other stats and HP. When the form hits 0 HP it reverts and takes back its old HP; leftover damage carries over. It can only do what the beast can, can't talk or cast spells, and its gear merges into the form, unusable.

An invisible 10 ft radius sphere of antimagic stays centred on you. Nobody can cast spells inside. Summoned or magically made creatures and objects wink out while in it, magic items act as mundane ones, and teleports or planar travel into or out of it fail; portals and extradimensional spaces close while inside.

Spells and magic effects in it, or aimed at something in it, are suppressed (artifacts and deities excepted), and their durations keep running. A slot spent on a suppressed spell is still used. Areas like fireball stop at its edge. A magic weapon is mundane against a target inside or in a wielder's hands inside. Dispel magic doesn't touch it, and two fields don't cancel.
antimagic-field.material: Powdered iron or iron filings (a pinch)

description: Choose a Huge or smaller creature or object, or up to a 200 ft cube, within 60 ft, and an intelligent creature type. For 10 days the target has one aura:
Antipathy: one that sees the target or comes within 60 ft makes a Wisdom save or is frightened while it sees it or is within 60 ft, fleeing to the nearest safe spot out of sight.
Sympathy: on a failed Wisdom save, it spends its movement each turn reaching the target and won't willingly leave. Harm from the target grants a save.
It saves again on ending a turn beyond 60 ft and out of sight, and every 24 hours; success frees it, then 1 minute of immunity.
antipathy-sympathy.material: Alum soaked in vinegar (antipathy) or a drop of honey (sympathy)

description: You and up to 8 willing creatures within 10 ft project into the Astral Plane (fails if you're already there). Bodies left behind lie unconscious in suspended animation, needing no food or air and not ageing.

Each astral form copies its owner's stats and gear and trails a silver cord; if an effect cuts the cord, that creature dies. Harm to the astral form doesn't reach the body. Entering another plane, or your starting one, through a portal pulls your body there to rejoin.
Your action ends it for all. It ends for one creature whose body or astral form hits 0 HP or is dispelled; the cord pulls it home. If you're returned early, the others stay.
astral-projection.material: Per creature: a jacinth worth 1,000 gp and a carved silver bar worth 100 gp, consumed

description: Grow a lifeless spare body of a living creature in a sealed vessel. In 120 days it reaches full adult size, or you can have it come out younger. It keeps indefinitely while the vessel is left alone.

After it matures, should the original die with a soul that is free and willing to come back, that soul moves in. The new body is a perfect physical match with the same personality, memories and abilities, though it has none of the old gear. The original's remains turn inert and can never be raised, because the soul now lives elsewhere.
clone.material: Diamond (1,000 gp+) and 1 cubic inch of the creature's flesh, both consumed; a vessel with a sealable lid big enough for a Medium creature (2,000 gp+)

description: A celestial of CR 4 or lower appears in an empty space you can see within 90 ft. It is friendly to you and your allies, rolls its own initiative, and follows your spoken orders (no action needed) unless they go against its alignment. With no orders, it only defends itself. It vanishes at 0 hp or when the spell ends. The DM has its stats.
conjure-celestial.higherLevels: With a 9th-level slot, the celestial can be CR 5 or lower.

description: You must be outdoors. For the duration you control the weather within 5 miles; going somewhere without open sky overhead ends it. When you cast it, you shift precipitation, temperature and wind each by one stage up or down (and can turn the wind). Changes take 1d4 × 10 minutes to arrive, then you can shift again. Once the spell is over, the weather slowly returns to normal.
Precipitation: clear (1), light clouds (2), overcast or fog (3), rain, hail or snow (4), torrential rain, heavy hail or blizzard (5).
Temperature: unbearable heat (1), hot (2), warm (3), cool (4), cold (5), arctic (6).
Wind: calm (1), moderate (2), strong (3), gale (4), storm (5).
control-weather.material: Incense burning, plus earth and wood bits in water

description: A glowing bead hangs at a point within 150 ft. When the spell ends (you drop concentration or choose to end it), it bursts in a 20 ft radius sphere that spreads around corners. Each creature there makes a Dexterity save: full fire damage on a failure, half on a success.
Damage starts at 12d6 and grows by 1d6 at the end of each of your turns it hasn't gone off.

A creature that touches the bead first makes a Dexterity save. On a failure it explodes at once; on a success the creature can throw it up to 40 ft, and it explodes when it hits a creature or solid object. The fire lights unattended flammable objects.
delayed-blast-fireball.higherLevels: Each slot level above 7 adds 1d6 to the base damage.
delayed-blast-fireball.material: A tiny ball of bat guano and sulfur

description: A shadowy door, big enough for Medium creatures, appears on a flat solid surface you can see within 60 ft. It opens onto an empty room of wood or stone, 30 ft in each dimension. When the spell ends, the door vanishes and anyone or anything inside is stuck there.
Each casting can make a new demiplane or link to one you made before. If you know what another caster's demiplane from this spell is like and holds, you can link to that one instead.
Any number of creatures of your choice within 30 ft that you can see and that can hear you make a Charisma save. On a failure, the effect depends on its current HP:
50 HP or less: deafened, 1 minute.
40 HP or less: blinded and deafened, 10 minutes.
30 HP or less: stunned, blinded and deafened, 1 hour.
20 HP or less: dies.
Whatever its HP, a celestial, elemental, fey or fiend that fails is also banished to its home plane unless already there, and can't come back to your plane for 24 hours except by wish.
A creature you can see within 60 ft makes a Wisdom save (advantage if you or your allies are fighting it) or is charmed by you for up to 1 hour (concentration).

While on the same plane, you can give it simple orders telepathically (no action needed) and it does its best to obey; with no new orders it defends itself. As an action, take full control until the end of your next turn: it does only what you choose, and you can spend your reaction to make it use its own.
Each time it takes damage it repeats the save, ending the spell on a success.
dominate-monster.higherLevels: With a 9th-level slot, concentration lasts up to 8 hours.

description: A 100 ft radius around a point within 500 ft becomes difficult terrain. Grounded concentrating creatures there make a Constitution save or lose concentration. On casting and at each turn's end while you concentrate, grounded creatures there make a Dexterity save or fall prone.
Fissures: as your next turn starts, 1d6 fissures (1d10 × 10 ft deep, 10 ft wide) open; anyone over one makes a Dexterity save or falls in. Structures above one collapse.

Structures take 50 bludgeoning on casting and at the start of your turns. One at 0 HP collapses: creatures within half its height make a Dexterity save or take 5d6 bludgeoning, fall prone and are buried (DC 20 Athletics to escape); success halves it.
earthquake.material: Dirt (a pinch), a rock fragment and some clay

description: For up to 8 hours (end it with an action) you're in the Border Ethereal, overlapping your plane. You can move in any direction, but up or down costs double. You see and hear your home plane in grey, out to 60 ft.
You only affect, and are affected by, creatures on the Ethereal Plane; others can't sense you without special magic. You move through objects of your home plane.

When it ends you return to your home plane where you are; if that space is filled, you're shunted to the nearest free space, taking force damage equal to twice the feet moved. It fails if cast on the Ethereal Plane or a plane not bordering it.
etherealness.higherLevels: Each slot level above 7 lets you bring up to 3 willing creatures (counting you) within 10 ft.

description: A creature you can see within 150 ft takes 4d6 psychic damage and makes an Intelligence save. On a failure, its Intelligence and Charisma become 1: it can't cast spells, use magic items, understand language or communicate in any sensible way, though it still knows, follows and protects its friends.
It saves again at the end of every 30 days, ending the spell on a success. Greater restoration, heal or wish also ends it.
feeblemind.material: A handful of clay, crystal, glass or mineral spheres

description: A creature you can see within 60 ft makes a Constitution save: 7d8 + 30 necrotic damage, half on a success.
A humanoid it kills rises at the start of your next turn as a zombie under your permanent command, carrying out your spoken orders as best it can.
Roaring flame fills up to ten 10 ft cubes within 150 ft, arranged as you like, each sharing a face with another. Each creature in them makes a Dexterity save: 7d10 fire, half on a success.
It damages objects and lights unattended flammable ones. You can leave plants in the area unharmed.

An invisible, immobile prison of force forms around an area within 100 ft, for 1 hour. Pick a cage, up to 20 ft a side with bars 1/2 inch thick and 1/2 inch apart, or a solid box, up to 10 ft a side, that stops all matter and spells going in or out.

Creatures wholly inside are trapped; anyone partly inside or too big is pushed out. A trapped creature can't leave by nonmagical means. Teleport or planar travel out needs a Charisma save first; on a failure that use is wasted. It also blocks ethereal travel, and dispel magic can't end it.
For 8 hours, a willing creature you touch can't be surprised and gains advantage on attacks, ability checks and saves. Attackers have disadvantage against it.
Casting it again before it ends ends the first casting at once.

A circular portal 5 to 20 ft across opens in an empty space you can see within 60 ft, linking to a precise spot on another plane, facing any way you choose. Only stepping through its front works; travellers appear in the nearest free space on the far side. Deities and planar rulers can stop it opening near them or in their realms.

If you speak a creature's true name (not a nickname or title) and it is on another plane, the portal opens beside it and pulls it through to your side. You gain no control over it; the DM decides what it does.
For 1 hour, whenever you make a Charisma check, you can swap the number rolled for a 15. Magic that checks whether you're telling the truth always says you are.

Holy light spreads 30 ft around you. Until it ends, creatures you pick in that radius when you cast it shed dim light out to 5 ft, gain advantage on every saving throw, and impose disadvantage on attacks made against them.
When a fiend or undead hits one of them with a melee attack, the attacker makes a Constitution save or is blinded until the spell ends.
holy-aura.material: A tiny reliquary worth 1,000 gp holding a holy relic (such as a scrap of a saint's robe)

description: A creature you can see within 30 ft makes a Wisdom save or is bound (success: immune to your recasts). Bound, it needs no air, food or drink and doesn't age; divination can't find or perceive it. Choose:
Burial: a force sphere deep underground; nothing passes, even by teleport or planar travel.
Chaining: restrained by rooted chains; it can't move or be moved.
Hedged Prison: a tiny demiplane warded against teleport and planar travel.
Minimus Containment: shrunk to 1 inch inside an unbreakable gem only light passes.
Slumber: an unwakeable sleep.
You may set a DM-approved, observable release condition. Only a 9th-level dispel magic on the prison or component ends it. Reusing a component frees its earlier prisoner.
imprisonment.material: A vellum picture or carved statuette of the target, plus a form-specific item worth 500 gp per Hit Die of the target (mithral orb, precious-metal chain, jade model of the prison, large clear gem, or rare sleep herbs)

description: A 20 ft radius sphere of smoke and white-hot embers fills a point within 150 ft. It spreads around corners, is heavily obscured, and lasts until a wind of 10 mph or more blows it away.
Each creature in it when it appears makes a Dexterity save: 10d8 fire, half on a success. Anyone entering it for the first time in a turn, or finishing a turn inside, saves too.
Each time your turn begins, the cloud drifts 10 ft straight away from you, in a direction you pick.

You split up to 700 HP of healing as you like among any number of creatures you can see within 60 ft. Each creature healed is also cured of every disease and of anything leaving it blinded or deafened. Undead and constructs are unaffected.

A creature you can see within 60 ft is banished to a labyrinth demiplane until the spell ends or it gets out. As its action it can try a DC 20 Intelligence check; success frees it and ends the spell (a minotaur or goristro demon always succeeds).
When the spell ends, it returns to the space it left, or the nearest free space if that one is taken.

Four blazing orbs slam into points you can see within 1 mile. Each creature in a 40 ft radius sphere around any point makes a Dexterity save: 20d6 fire plus 20d6 bludgeoning, half on a success. A creature caught in several blasts is hit only once.
The blasts spread around corners, damage objects, and set alight flammable objects nobody is wearing or carrying.

For 24 hours, the willing creature you touch can't take psychic damage and is immune to the charmed condition, to divination spells, and to anything that would sense its emotions or read its thoughts. Even wish and magic of that power can't touch its mind or gather information about it.

Disguise up to a 1 mile square of land as some other terrain for 10 days. It looks, sounds, smells and even feels different, but keeps its basic shape: a road might pass for a swamp, a pond for a meadow, a cliff for an easy slope. Buildings can be altered or invented too. Creatures can't be hidden, disguised or added.

Since the mirage can be touched, it really slows or blocks travel: open ground may become difficult terrain, or rough ground easy going. Any bit of it taken out of the area vanishes. Truesight shows the real land, yet the rest of the illusion still affects that viewer, who can still touch it.

For 24 hours an extradimensional home exists within 300 ft, with one shimmering entrance 5 ft wide and 10 ft tall where you choose. You and creatures you name at casting can enter while it's open. Within 30 ft of it you can open or close it; closed, it is invisible.

Inside is a grand foyer and rooms up to 50 cubes of 10 ft each, laid out and furnished as you wish, with food for a nine-course feast for up to 100 people. 100 near-transparent servants obey you but can't attack or harm anyone, and can't leave. Objects taken outside turn to smoke. When it ends, everyone inside is expelled near the entrance.
mordenkainens-magnificent-mansion.material: A miniature ivory portal, a bit of polished marble and a small silver spoon, 5 gp each

description: Summon a hovering blade of force within 60 ft that lasts up to 1 minute. As it appears, make a melee spell attack on a target within 5 ft of the blade, dealing 3d10 force if it hits.
While it lasts, your bonus action each turn flies the blade up to 20 ft to any visible spot and swings again, at the old target or a new one.
mordenkainens-sword.material: A tiny platinum sword with a copper and zinc grip and pommel, worth 250 gp

description: You and up to 8 willing creatures holding hands in a circle travel to another plane. Name a destination in broad terms (a city or palace) and you arrive in or near it, at the DM's call. If you know a teleportation circle's sigil sequence on another plane, you can arrive there instead; anyone who doesn't fit lands in the nearest free spaces.
Banish: make a melee spell attack against a creature you can reach. On a hit it makes a Charisma save; on a failure it lands at a random spot on a plane you name and must find its own way back.
plane-shift.material: A forked metal rod worth 250 gp, attuned to a plane

description: A creature you touch regains all its HP. If it is charmed, frightened, paralyzed or stunned, that condition ends, and a prone target may stand up using its reaction. No effect on undead or constructs.
Name a creature you can see within 60 ft. If its current HP is 100 or less, it dies on the spot. Otherwise nothing happens.

Name a creature you can see within 60 ft. If its current HP is 150 or less, it is stunned; otherwise nothing happens. It makes a Constitution save as each of its turns ends, shaking off the stun on a success.
Eight coloured rays fill a 60 ft cone. Each creature there makes a Dexterity save; roll a d8 per creature for its ray. Rays 1-5 deal 10d6, half on a success.
1: Red, fire.
2: Orange, acid.
3: Yellow, lightning.
4: Green, poison.
5: Blue, cold.
6: Indigo. Restrained on a failure; it makes a Constitution save at each turn's end. Three successes end it; three failures petrify it permanently (needn't be consecutive).
7: Violet. Blinded on a failure; a Wisdom save at the start of your next turn ends it, while a failure sends it, sighted again, to another plane of the DM's choice.
8: Two rays hit it: roll the d8 two more times, rerolling 8s.

An opaque wall of light, up to 90 ft long, 30 ft high and 1 inch thick (or a sphere up to 30 ft across), stands within 60 ft for 10 minutes; placing it through a creature wastes the spell. Bright light 100 ft, dim 100 ft beyond. You and chosen creatures pass through safely.

Others that see it and come within 20 ft or start a turn there make a Constitution save or are blinded for 1 minute. Passing or reaching through takes a Dexterity save per layer; layers 1-5 deal half on a success. Layers fall in order. A rod of cancellation destroys it; antimagic field doesn't.
1: Red. 10d6 fire; blocks nonmagical ranged attacks. Destroyed by 25 cold.
2: Orange. 10d6 acid; blocks magical ranged attacks. Destroyed by strong wind.
3: Yellow. 10d6 lightning. Destroyed by 60 force.
4: Green. 10d6 poison. Destroyed by passwall or an equal portal spell.
5: Blue. 10d6 cold. Destroyed by 25 fire.
6: Indigo. Restrained; Constitution save each turn end, three successes free it, three failures petrify it. Blocks spells. Destroyed by daylight or equal.
7: Violet. Blinded; Wisdom save at the start of your next turn or sent to another plane. Destroyed by dispel magic or equal.

An intangible illusory copy of you appears anywhere within 500 miles that you have seen before, whatever lies between. It looks and sounds like you and mimics your mannerisms. It vanishes, ending the spell, if it takes any damage.

Your action moves it up to double your speed and lets it gesture, talk and act however you like. As a bonus action you switch between its senses and yours; while using its eyes and ears you are blinded and deafened to your own surroundings.
Touch shows it's fake. A creature that spends its action studying it sees through it with a successful Intelligence (Investigation) check vs your spell save DC.
project-image.material: A small replica of you made of materials worth 5 gp

description: A creature you touch regains 4d8 + 15 HP, then 1 HP whenever its turn starts, for 1 hour (10 HP per minute).
Severed body parts (fingers, legs, tails…) grow back after 2 minutes. If you hold the severed part to the stump, it reattaches at once.
regenerate.material: A prayer wheel and holy water

description: A creature you touch that has been dead at most a century, didn't die of old age and isn't undead returns with full HP if its soul is free and willing.
It is cured of poisons and normal diseases, its mortal wounds close and lost body parts regrow. Magical diseases, curses and the like persist unless removed first.
It takes -4 on attack rolls, saves and ability checks, easing by 1 per long rest.
If it had been dead a year or more, you can't cast spells and have disadvantage on attacks, ability checks and saves until you finish a long rest.

Gravity flips in a 50 ft radius, 100 ft high cylinder centred on a point within 100 ft. Every unanchored creature and object there falls upward to the top when you cast it. A creature can make a Dexterity save to grab a fixed object within reach and avoid falling.

Anything that hits a ceiling or other solid object on the way takes normal falling damage. Anything that reaches the top without hitting something hovers there, swaying slightly. When the spell ends, everything drops back down.

Until dispelled, a willing creature or an object you touch turns invisible, and divination can't target it nor scrying sensors perceive it. A creature falls into suspended animation: time stops for it and it doesn't age.
You can set an ending condition, anything that happens or can be seen within 1 mile of the target ("after 1,000 years"). Any damage to the target also ends it.
sequester.material: Diamond, emerald, ruby and sapphire dust worth 5,000 gp, consumed

description: You turn into a creature with CR up to your level that you've seen: an average one (no class levels or Spellcasting), not a construct or undead.

Its stats replace yours, except alignment, Int, Wis and Cha. You keep your skill and save proficiencies, add its own, and use its bonus where higher. No legendary or lair actions. You take its HP and Hit Dice; at 0 HP you revert, excess damage carrying over.
Class, race and other features work if the body allows; you lose special senses it lacks; you speak only if it can. Gear falls, merges or is worn (DM rules on fit).
Your action switches to another valid form; your HP can't rise from it.
shapechange.material: A jade circlet worth 1,500 gp, put on your head before casting

description: You build an illusory copy of a beast or humanoid that stays within reach for the whole casting. It is part real, made of ice or snow, and acts as a normal creature with the original's stats, but has half its hit point maximum and no gear.

It is friendly to you and creatures you name, obeys your spoken orders and acts on your turn in combat. It can't learn, level up or regain spent spell slots. You can repair it in an alchemical lab with herbs and minerals costing 100 gp per HP. At 0 HP it melts away. Casting this again destroys any simulacrum you already have.
simulacrum.material: Enough snow or ice for a life-size copy, some hair or nail of the creature placed inside, and powdered ruby worth 1,500 gp (consumed)

description: A storm cloud, 360 ft in radius, gathers over a point you can see. As it forms, each creature under it (within 5,000 ft) makes a Constitution save or takes 2d6 thunder and is deafened for 5 minutes. On your turn each round you concentrate:
Round 2: acid rain, 1d6 acid to everything below.
Round 3: six bolts at six different targets you choose below; Dexterity save, 10d6 lightning, half on a success.
Round 4: hail, 2d6 bludgeoning to everything below.
Rounds 5-10: icy rain and wind. Difficult terrain, heavily obscured, 1d6 cold to each creature, no ranged weapon attacks, severe distraction for concentration; fog and mist are blown off.

Sunlight blazes in a 60 ft radius around a point within 150 ft. Each creature in it makes a Constitution save: 12d6 radiant and blinded for 1 minute, or half damage and not blinded on a success. Undead and oozes save with disadvantage.
A blinded creature saves again as each of its turns ends, regaining sight on a success. Darkness from spells in the area is dispelled.
sunburst.material: Fire and a piece of sunstone

description: You inscribe a near-invisible glyph on a surface (up to 10 ft across) or inside a closable object (moving it over 10 ft ends the spell). Spotting it needs an Intelligence (Investigation) check vs your spell save DC. You choose the trigger, can refine it, and can exempt creatures (e.g. a password).
Triggered, it sheds dim light in a 60 ft radius for 10 minutes, then ends. Creatures there, or entering or ending a turn there, suffer one effect:
Death: Constitution save, 10d10 necrotic, half on a success.
Discord: Constitution save or 1 minute of bickering: no useful talk, disadvantage on attacks and ability checks.
Fear: Wisdom save or frightened 1 minute, dropping held items and moving 30 ft away each turn.
Hopelessness: Charisma save or 1 minute unable to attack or harm anyone.
Insanity: Intelligence save or 1 minute insane: no actions, no reading or understanding, erratic DM-run movement.
Pain: Constitution save or incapacitated 1 minute.
Sleep: Wisdom save or unconscious 10 minutes; damage or a shake wakes it.
Stunning: Wisdom save or stunned 1 minute.
symbol.material: Mercury, phosphorus, and powdered diamond and opal worth 1,000 gp in total, consumed

description: For 24 hours you share a telepathic link with a willing creature you know, anywhere on your plane. It ends if either of you leaves that plane.
You can trade words, images, sounds and other sensations at once, and it knows it's you. Any creature with Intelligence 1 or more understands your words and the sense of what you send.
telepathy.material: A pair of linked silver rings

description: You and up to 8 willing creatures, or one object (fits a 10 ft cube, not held by an unwilling creature), all within 10 ft and seen, go to a known destination on your plane. The DM rolls d100:
Permanent circle, associated object: on target.
Very familiar: mishap 01-05, similar 06-13, off 14-24, on 25-100.
Seen casually: mishap 01-33, similar 34-43, off 44-53, on 54-100.
Viewed once, description: mishap 01-43, similar 44-53, off 54-73, on 74-100.
False destination: mishap 01-50, similar 51-100.
Off target: 1d10 × 1d10 percent of the distance away, random direction. Similar area: a look-alike place anywhere on the plane. Mishap: 3d10 force to each traveller, then the DM rolls again.
Time halts for everyone else. You get 1d4 + 1 consecutive turns, acting and moving as normal.
It ends early if any action you take or effect you create in that time affects another creature or an object someone else wears or carries, or if you move more than 1,000 ft from where you cast it.

Choose a creature or an unworn, uncarried nonmagical object you can see within 30 ft. Unwilling creatures make a Wisdom save; shapechangers are immune. It lasts until the spell ends or the target hits 0 HP, and becomes permanent if you concentrate the full hour.
Creature to creature: CR up to the target's (or its level). New stats, same alignment and personality, new HP; at 0 HP it reverts, excess carrying over. It acts only as the form allows; gear merges.
Object to creature: no bigger than the object, CR 9 or lower; friendly, acts on your turns as you direct; uncontrolled once permanent.
Creature to object: it and its gear become the object; afterwards it remembers nothing.
true-polymorph.material: A drop of mercury, some gum arabic and a wisp of smoke

description: A creature you touch that died no more than 200 years ago, of anything but old age, returns with full HP if its soul is free and willing. All wounds close, poison and disease are cured, any curses it had at death are lifted, and missing organs and limbs are replaced.
If the body is gone, speak the creature's name: it reappears in a new body in a free space of your choice within 10 ft.
true-resurrection.material: Holy water and diamonds worth 25,000 gp, consumed

description: A wall of water up to 300 ft long, 300 ft high and 50 ft thick rises at a point you can see. Each creature in it makes a Strength save: 6d10 bludgeoning, half on a success.

As each of your turns begins, it rolls 50 ft away from you with everyone inside. Each Huge or smaller creature inside or in its path makes a Strength save or takes 5d10 bludgeoning (once per round). Then it loses 50 ft of height and later damage drops 1d10; at 0 ft it ends.
Swimming in it needs a Strength (Athletics) check vs your spell save DC. Leaving it, a creature falls.
Each creature in a 30 ft radius sphere around a point within 120 ft makes a Wisdom save or is frightened by phantoms of its worst fears that only it can see, until the spell ends.
At the start of each of its turns, a frightened creature makes a Wisdom save or takes 4d10 psychic damage. A success ends the spell for it.
Copy any spell of 8th level or lower, ignoring all requirements, even costly materials. Or pick one:
• A nonmagical object worth up to 25,000 gp, at most 300 ft in any dimension, appears on the ground in view.
• Up to 20 creatures you can see regain all HP and lose every effect greater restoration ends.
• Up to 10 creatures you can see gain resistance to one damage type.
• Up to 10 creatures you can see become immune to one spell or effect for 8 hours.
• Force a reroll of any one roll from the last round (your last turn included), optionally with advantage or disadvantage; you pick which result stands.
Other wishes: tell the DM; bigger ones risk failure or twisted results.

Any use besides copying a spell strains you: until a long rest, each spell you cast deals you 1d10 necrotic per spell level (unpreventable); your Strength drops to 3 for 2d4 days (2 days fewer per day of rest); 33 percent chance you lose wish forever.
Pick a nonmagical flame you can see within range that fits in a 5-ft cube, then choose one effect:
• Spread it 5 ft in one direction, if wood or other fuel is there.
• Snuff out the flames in the cube.
• For 1 hour, double or halve its bright and dim light, change its color, or both.
• For 1 hour, simple moving shapes (a creature, an object, a place) dance in it.
Up to 3 of the lasting effects at once; dismiss one as an action.

A magic bonfire fills a 5-ft cube of visible ground within range for the duration. A creature there when it appears makes a Dexterity save or takes 1d8 fire damage. A creature also saves on first entering the space during a turn, and when it ends its turn there.
It sets alight flammable objects in the area that nobody is wearing or carrying.
Damage rises to 2d8 at level 5, 3d8 at level 11 and 4d8 at level 17.

Numbing frost forms on a creature you can see within range. It makes a Constitution save; on a failure it takes 1d6 cold damage and has disadvantage on its next weapon attack roll before its next turn ends.
Damage rises to 2d6 at level 5, 3d6 at level 11 and 4d6 at level 17.
Bend the air at a visible point within range to make one effect:
• Push: a Medium or smaller creature you choose makes a Strength save or is shoved up to 5 ft away from you.
• Shove: an object of up to 5 pounds that nobody holds or carries slides up to 10 ft away from you, too gently to deal damage.
• Breeze: a harmless effect, such as rustling leaves, slamming shutters or rippling clothes.

Mites and fleas swarm over a creature you can see within range. It makes a Constitution save or takes 1d6 poison damage and is driven 5 ft in a random direction, but only if it is able to move and its speed is 5 ft or more. Roll a d4: 1 north, 2 south, 3 east, 4 west. The move provokes no opportunity attacks, and if that way is blocked it stays put.
Damage rises to 2d6 at level 5, 3d6 at level 11 and 4d6 at level 17.

Touch 1 to 3 pebbles to charge them. You or anyone else can make a ranged spell attack by throwing one (range 60 ft) or slinging it. Another attacker adds your spellcasting modifier to the attack roll, not their own.
A hit deals 1d6 + your spellcasting modifier bludgeoning damage. Hit or miss, that pebble loses its magic. Casting the spell again ends it on any pebbles left from before.
Pick dirt or stone you can see within range that fits in a 5-ft cube, then choose one effect:
• Dig: instantly scoop out loose earth and drop it up to 5 ft away, too gently to deal damage.
• Mark: shapes, colors or both appear on it, forming words, pictures or patterns, for 1 hour.
• Terrain: ground there turns into difficult terrain, or difficult terrain turns normal, for 1 hour.
Up to 2 of the lasting effects at once; dismiss one as an action.
Your teeth or nails grow sharp and corrosive. Make a melee spell attack against a creature within 5 ft of you; a hit deals 1d10 acid damage. Afterwards your teeth or nails go back to normal.
Damage rises to 2d10 at level 5, 3d10 at level 11 and 4d10 at level 17.
Pick water you can see within range that fits in a 5-ft cube, then choose one effect:
• Flow: instantly move it or redirect its flow up to 5 ft in any direction, too gently to deal damage.
• Shapes: it forms simple shapes that move as you direct, for 1 hour.
• Tint: change its color or opacity evenly, for 1 hour.
• Freeze: it turns to ice if no creature is in it, and thaws after 1 hour.
Up to 2 of the lasting effects at once; dismiss one as an action.
A booming crack, audible 100 ft away, bursts from you. Every other creature within 5 ft makes a Constitution save or takes 1d6 thunder damage.
Damage rises to 2d6 at level 5, 3d6 at level 11 and 4d6 at level 17.
A mournful bell tolls around a creature you can see within range. It makes a Wisdom save or takes 1d8 necrotic damage, or 1d12 if it is already missing any hit points.
Damage rises to 2d8 (2d12) at level 5, 3d8 (3d12) at level 11 and 4d8 (4d12) at level 17.
You speak a holy word and searing light bursts from you. Each creature you choose that you can see within 5 ft makes a Constitution save or takes 1d6 radiant damage.
Damage rises to 2d6 at level 5, 3d6 at level 11 and 4d6 at level 17.
Reaction when acid, cold, fire, lightning or thunder damage hits you. You resist that damage type, the triggering hit included, until your next turn starts.
On your next turn, your first melee hit adds 1d6 damage of that type to the target, and then the spell ends.
absorb-elements.higherLevels: The extra damage rises by 1d6 for each slot level above 1.

description: Touch a beast that is charmed by you or friendly toward you to link minds with it; the spell fails if its Intelligence is 4 or higher. While you can see each other, it understands your telepathic messages and can send back simple feelings and ideas.
While the link holds, the beast has advantage on attack rolls against creatures you can see within 5 ft of you.
Pick an object of 1 to 5 pounds in range that nobody is wearing or carrying. It flies up to 90 ft in a straight line in a direction you choose, stopping early if it meets a solid surface.
A creature in its path makes a Dexterity save. On a failure, the object strikes it and stops, and both take 3d8 bludgeoning damage.
catapult.higherLevels: Each slot level above 1 adds 5 pounds to the weight limit and 1d8 to the damage.
